pll2d15c9-d1e3519.summary: States that all things were naturally good and without vice; each is good and all together very good, since from all arises the universe's admirable beauty, in which even evil, well ordered, commends the good. So on the sixth day all works were consummated.
claims: Creation is good in each part and very good as a whole.
Evil rightly ordered commends the good.

pll2d15c9-d1e3542.summary: Asks how, then, God completed his work on the seventh day, as the Hebrew reads, though he created nothing new; perhaps because he blessed and sanctified it, since blessing and sanctifying are works, as Solomon did a work in dedicating the temple.
claims: God's blessing and sanctifying the seventh day is a work.

pl-l2d15c9.summary: States that all things were good by nature, without vice; each is good and all together very good, since the beauty of the universe arises from all, and even evil, rightly ordered, commends the good (Augustine). The consummation was on the sixth day. So how did God complete his work on the seventh day, as the Hebrew has? Perhaps because he blessed and sanctified it, which is a work, as Solomon did something in dedicating the temple.
claims: All created things were naturally good.
All things together are very good.
Evil rightly ordered commends the good.
Creation was consummated on the sixth day.
God 'completed' on the seventh day by blessing and sanctifying it.
